restatements.text: Requires all county jails to hold individuals named in federal immigration detainer requests for up to 48 hours beyond their otherwise scheduled release time.

analysis.answer: Under current law, each county decides for itself whether to honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure removes that local discretion, requiring every county jail to honor the requests and hold the named individuals for up to 48 hours past their normal release time.

Counties will face direct costs to house, feed, and secure individuals for up to 48 additional hours per detainer. Counties may also incur legal costs or liability if individuals sue over wrongful detention or constitutional claims related to being held on administrative detainers without a judicial warrant.

County governments and local taxpayers bear the financial burden of the extended detention and potential litigation. Federal immigration enforcement agencies benefit from having individuals securely held at local expense until they can be transferred.

Facing mandatory holds, individuals in immigrant communities may become less likely to report crimes, serve as witnesses, or interact with local police out of fear that any jail booking could lead to deportation. Some counties might look for ways to expedite releases before a federal detainer can be formalized.

The measure addresses the issue of individuals with federal immigration detainers being released from local custody into the community. The mechanism addresses this directly by imposing a blanket mandate on county jails to hold those individuals. However, it may create spillover costs in the form of eroded trust between local law enforcement and immigrant communities.

State government gains power over local jail policies. Federal immigration authorities gain leverage and guaranteed cooperation from local jurisdictions. County governments and locally elected sheriffs lose discretionary power over their own jail populations.

It is empirically disputed whether local cooperation with immigration enforcement improves public safety. Some studies find that it reduces crime by removing offenders, while others find that it decreases public safety by discouraging immigrant communities from reporting incidents and cooperating with local police.

flags.quote: Every county jail shall honor a detainer request from federal immigration authorities by holding the named person for up to 48 hours
flags.note: The measure mandates that counties pay for up to 48 hours of additional jail operations per request without providing state funding to cover the costs.
